4.1.17 Shortcomings in e-Vouchers

IFHRMS aimed at paperless and hassle free environment for carrying out Government transactions. Submission of e-vouchers in lieu of physical vouchers would help achieve this to a large extent. Analysis of e-vouchers generated online through IFHRMS revealed the following:

46

Chapter IV - Processing of Bills

 e-vouchers did not carry digital signature for testifying its authenticity and for non-repudiation. All DDOs were required to manually sign the printouts of bills generated in IFHRMS before submission to PAO/Treasury.

 e-vouchers and related sub-vouchers were not dated and time stamped by DDOs and did not contain all information2 as in physical vouchers.

 Scanned copies of all supporting documents viz., sub-vouchers, sanction orders, etc., were not available for all e-vouchers, as most DDOs did not scan them while submitting bills online in IFHRMS.

Thus, e-vouchers did not meet all legal requirements for acceptance and Department has a long way to go to reach its goal of moving to paperless and hassle free environment for carrying out Government transactions.

Government replied (January 2023) that printing the details of Digital Signature in the bills would be enabled at the earliest and on stabilization of the system the physical copies would be dispensed with in a phased manner and that instructions have been issued to ensure attachment of scanned copies of all sub-vouchers.

4.2 Pension Management System

Pension Management System had inaccurate date of birth details which delayed sanction of additional pension to eligible pensioners and allowed creation of multiple pensioner IDs for the same pensioner leading to double pension payment. Further, incorrect mapping of pensioner ID to pension pay order prevented pensioners from logging into IFHRMS for updating basic personal information like bank details, address, etc.

In pre-IFHRMS scenario, e-Pension software, a web based application, was used for generating monthly pension after processing pension payment orders received physically from AG (A&E). Any person aggrieved by a decision or order of the Planning Authority under Section 49 or sub-section (1) of Section 54 of the Act may prefer an appeal before the prescribed Appellate Authority.

The appeal shall be filed within two months from the date of communication of the decision or order. However, the Appellate Authority may admit an appeal filed after the prescribed period, if satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal within the stipulated time.

Upon receipt of the appeal, the Appellate Authority shall, through the portal, call for the remarks of the concerned Planning Authority and may also seek additional documents’ or clarifications from the appellant, wherever necessary.

Bilkkal - Jawalagiri Elephant Corridor

WHEREAS the Government of Tamil Nadu is deeply committed to the conservation of Asiatic Elephants and need to notify elephant corridors, so as to ensure the unobstructed movement of Asian Elephants (Elephas maximus), long-term survival of the species and to mitigate human-Wildlife conflict;

AND WHEREAS a Committee has been constituted by the Government vide G.O(D) No. 296, Environment, Climate Change and Forests (FR.5) Department dated 26.12.2022, to identify and delineate the corridors and the Committee has submitted its report through Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Chief Wildlife Warden of the State;

AND WHEREAS, for the above said purposes, the Government of Tamil Nadu after careful consideration of the said report have decided to notify the areas mentioned in the Schedule below as Bilikkal — Jawalagiri Corridor with effect from the date of publication of this notification.

THE SCHEDULE. I. Name of the Elephant Corridor: Bilikkal — Jawalagiri II. Description of the critical Elephant Corridor

This corridor is a part of Jawalgiri Reserved Forest, starts and ends in Jawalagiri Reserved Forest of Cauvery North Wildlife Sanctuary by connecting two large habitats i.e. Jawalagiri Reserved Forest (Jawalagiri Range) in Cauvery North Wildlife Sanctuary, Tamil Nadu and _ Bilikkal State Forest in Bannerghatta National Park, Karnataka State. The length of the elephant corridor is 2.20 km and the width ranges from 0.66 km to 1.50 km. The given route is regular elephant movement by connecting above two large habitats. Benki falls and other small streams are falling in the Jawalagiri Reserved Forest. This route will enable the Trans-Cauvery migration of Elephants and other large mammals between the States of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. There is No bottleneck located in this corridor.
